full_text_en:
LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO CORPORATION v. Dexing Shipping Co., Ltd., Hainan Qinglong Shipping Enterprise General Corporation and its Guangzhou Branch — Maritime Fraud Dispute

Plaintiff: LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO CORPORATION (Philippines).

Legal Representative: Alfonso A. Uy, President of the corporation.

Agents ad litem: Lü Jianeng and Zou Weining, lawyers of Beijing Jun He Law Firm.

Defendant: Panama Dexing Shipping Co., Ltd.

Defendant: Hainan Qinglong Shipping Enterprise General Corporation.

Legal Representative: Zhong Liang, Chairman of the corporation.

Defendant: Hainan Qinglong Shipping Enterprise General Corporation, Guangzhou Branch.

Legal Representative: Liu Xuelan, Manager of the branch.

Agents ad litem for the above two defendants: Hu Zhengliang and Cao Chong, professors and graduate students of Dalian Maritime University.

The plaintiff, LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO CORPORATION (hereinafter referred to as "LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO"), filed an action with the Guangzhou Maritime Court against the defendants Panama Dexing Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Dexing"), Hainan Qinglong Shipping Enterprise General Corporation (hereinafter referred to as "Qinglong Head Office"), and Hainan Qinglong Shipping Enterprise General Corporation, Guangzhou Branch (hereinafter referred to as "Qinglong Branch") concerning a maritime fraud infringement dispute.

The plaintiff, LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO, alleged: The defendant Dexing, in its capacity as the registered shipowner, forged bills of lading and sold a batch of cargo loaded by the plaintiff on the vessel "Golden Sun" to others. The defendant Qinglong Head Office is the actual owner of the "Golden Sun", and the defendant Qinglong Branch is the actual operator of the "Golden Sun". Qinglong Head Office verified the forged bills of lading issued by Dexing, and Qinglong Branch stamped and endorsed the forged bills of lading to confirm their validity. The actions of the two defendants constituted joint infringement with Dexing. The plaintiff requested the court to order the three defendants to return the cargo with a total purchase value of USD 1,690,000 and to compensate for all economic losses caused thereby.

The defendant Qinglong Head Office argued: The party that entered into a voyage charter party with RADIANT Shipping Company of Athens, Greece, the charterer of the "Golden Sun" for this voyage, was the shipowner of the "Golden Sun" and the defendant Dexing. Qinglong Head Office is neither the actual owner of the "Golden Sun" nor has any relationship with the vessel. The fax bearing the letterhead of Qinglong Head Office submitted by the plaintiff to the court was sent by Qinglong Branch using Qinglong Head Office's notepaper; it was not sent by Qinglong Head Office and should not be binding on Qinglong Head Office. The plaintiff's claim that the freight involved in this case was collected by Qinglong Head Office and that Qinglong Head Office verified the second set of bills of lading issued by Dexing is inconsistent with the facts. The plaintiff has been unable to prove that Qinglong Head Office had subjective fraudulent intent or objectively committed fraudulent acts. Therefore, Qinglong Head Office should not bear any liability. The plaintiff's lawsuit against Qinglong Head Office is without legal basis or factual grounds and should be dismissed.

The defendant Qinglong Branch argued: There is a shipping agency relationship between Qinglong Branch and the defendant Dexing, not a ship charter relationship. Qinglong Branch was authorized by Dexing to urge and collect freight on its behalf and to verify bills of lading on its behalf. When Qinglong Branch verified bills of lading for Dexing, it did not know that the bill of lading was forged. Qinglong Branch had no malicious intent to defraud the plaintiff and had no connection with the fraud against the plaintiff. Qinglong Branch merely performed its duties as an agent of Dexing. It had neither subjective intent to defraud the plaintiff nor objectively committed any act of fraud. The court should dismiss the plaintiff's claims against Qinglong Branch.

The defendant Dexing did not respond to the action.

After trial, the Guangzhou Maritime Court found the following facts:

On July 18, 1997, the plaintiff LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO purchased 12,002 metric tons of urea from Sinochem (UK) Co., Ltd. at a price of USD 141 per metric ton. The shipper, CHINEXPORT of Sofia, Bulgaria, loaded the cargo on board the "Golden Sun" at the port of Odessa, Ukraine, and paid freight to RADIANT Company, the charterer for the voyage, for carriage from Odessa, Ukraine to Iloilo, Philippines. On August 18, 1997, COSCO Odessa Shipping and Trading Co., Ltd., as the ship's agent for the "Golden Sun", issued a set of original clean shipped bills of lading numbered 4407010021799. The bill of lading stated: shipper as AZOT of Novomoskovsk, Russia; consignee as "to order of Philippine Islands Bank"; vessel as "Golden Sun"; port of loading as Odessa, Ukraine; port of discharge as Iloilo, Philippines; shipowner as the defendant Dexing; description and quantity of cargo as 12,002 metric tons of urea; freight as "payable as per charter party". The seller, Sinochem (UK), received the bill of lading on the same day.

The defendant Dexing had previously issued a power of attorney to the defendant Qinglong Branch on June 30, 1997. The power of attorney stated: Qinglong Branch is hereby authorized as our agent to handle on our behalf the appointment of loading and discharging port agents, arrangement of fresh water, fuel, and supplies, urging and collection of freight, and other necessary agency matters for the "Golden Sun" on voyages between Europe and Southeast Asia or China routes. On August 20, 1997, and October 14, 1997, employees of Qinglong Branch, Xing Dezhang and Jiao Changren, sent faxes to RADIANT Company, the voyage charterer of the "Golden Sun", using notepaper bearing the letterhead of the defendant Qinglong Head Office, demanding payment of freight for the voyage in question. The telephone number from which the faxes were sent was the number of Qinglong Branch.

On September 30, 1997, after the plaintiff LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO paid the full purchase price of USD 1,692,282 for the 12,002 metric tons of urea, it took delivery from the bank of the full set of original bills of lading for the cargo, endorsed by Philippine Islands Bank, and awaited the arrival of the "Golden Sun" at Iloilo, Philippines for discharge. Under normal calculations, the voyage would have taken approximately one month. However, by December 1997, the "Golden Sun" had not arrived at the intended port and had lost contact with the shipper and consignee.

On December 11, 1997, the defendant Dexing, as seller, entered into a contract with Yaquan International Co., Ltd., agreeing that Dexing would sell 12,002 metric tons of urea to Yaquan International at a price of USD 90 per net metric ton, CIF Zhanjiang. To perform this contract, Dexing issued a second set of bills of lading for the cargo in question. The bill of lading recorded the same shipper, description and quantity of cargo, date of issue, carrying vessel, and port of loading as the bill of lading issued at Odessa. However, the notification address recorded on this set of bills of lading was Zhanjiang Port Authority Shipping and Freight Forwarding Company, No. 1 Renmin Road, Xiashan, Zhanjiang, with contact person Yang Baogui; the place of issue was Hong Kong; the port of discharge was Zhanjiang Port; and the issuer of the bills of lading was Dexing. In accordance with this instruction from Dexing, the "Golden Sun" discharged the 12,002 metric tons of urea it had carried at Zhanjiang Port on December 19, 1997.

On December 17, 1997, Yaquan International Co., Ltd., through Zhanjiang Port Authority Shipping and Freight Forwarding Company, went to Zhanjiang Ocean Shipping Agency to go through the procedures for taking delivery of the cargo. Because the bill of lading issued by the defendant Dexing was not endorsed by the shipper, Zhanjiang Ocean Shipping Agency faxed a copy of the bill of lading to the defendant Qinglong Branch, requesting Qinglong Branch to confirm whether the cargo could be released against that bill of lading. On the same day, Dexing sent a fax to Qinglong Branch stating: Please see the attached copy of the copy bill of lading. This is the bill of lading issued for this voyage of the "Golden Sun". Please confirm the original bill of lading presented by the consignee against this copy. We hereby confirm that you may release the cargo against this original bill of lading. The next day, Qinglong Branch stamped and endorsed the copy of the bill of lading faxed by Zhanjiang Ocean Shipping Agency with the notation: "This bill of lading is valid. Agree to release cargo." However, Yaquan International ultimately was unable to take delivery of the cargo against the bill of lading issued by Dexing, and accordingly filed an action with the Zhanjiang Intermediate People's Court, requesting that Dexing return the purchase price it had paid or deliver the cargo. On December 30, 1997, upon the application of Yaquan International, the Zhanjiang Intermediate People's Court sealed up the urea in this case at Zhanjiang Port. Because the customs formalities for this batch of urea had not yet been completed, it was under the supervision of Zhanjiang Customs.

On January 8, 1998, the plaintiff LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO filed an application for property preservation with the Guangzhou Maritime Court, requesting the arrest of the "Golden Sun", owned by the defendant Dexing, which was lying at Ningbo Port. The Guangzhou Maritime Court granted the application and sent personnel to Ningbo on January 9, 1998, to execute the order. Because the "Golden Sun" had already been arrested by the Ningbo Maritime Court, the Guangzhou Maritime Court immediately terminated the execution of the order, but incurred preservation application fees and execution costs of USD 9,520.

In June 1998, in accordance with the provisions of the Customs Law of the People's Republic of China, Zhanjiang Customs auctioned off the urea in this case, which was under its supervision, and preserved the proceeds, to be dealt with after the court determines the ownership of the cargo.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: the contract for the plaintiff's purchase of 12,002 metric tons of urea from Sinochem (UK) Co., Ltd.; the original clean bill of lading issued by COSCO Odessa Shipping and Trading Co., Ltd. as agent for the "Golden Sun"; the contract for the sale of 12,002 metric tons of urea between Dexing and Yaquan International Co., Ltd.; the bill of lading issued by Dexing to Yaquan International Co., Ltd.; the fax of December 17, 1997, in which Dexing confirmed that Qinglong Branch could release the cargo against the bill of lading held by Yaquan International; the copy of the bill of lading stamped by Qinglong Branch on December 18, 1997, with notation agreeing that Zhanjiang Ocean Shipping Agency could release the cargo; the power of attorney of June 30, 1997, in which Dexing entrusted Qinglong Branch to handle the operation of the "Golden Sun" on its behalf; the fax of December 10, 1997, in which Dexing entrusted Qinglong Branch to confirm bills of lading and release cargo on its behalf during the "Golden Sun's" call at Zhanjiang Port; two labor contracts between Qinglong Branch and Jiao Changren and Xing Dezhang; faxes sent by Xing Dezhang and Jiao Changren to RADIANT Company demanding payment of freight; and the statements of the parties.

The Guangzhou Maritime Court held:

This case is a foreign-related maritime fraud infringement dispute. The parties did not agree on the applicable law for resolving the substantive dispute. Pursuant to Article 146 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 29 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, because the infringing act in this case occurred in Zhanjiang, China, the Guangzhou Maritime Court has jurisdiction and Chinese law shall apply.

The plaintiff LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO paid the purchase price to Sinochem (UK) Co., Ltd. and took delivery of the bill of lading endorsed by the bank from the bank. Therefore, the plaintiff is the lawful holder of the bill of lading in this case and has an undisputable right of ownership over the cargo under the bill of lading. When its right of ownership over the cargo is infringed, it is entitled to claim compensation for losses caused thereby from the infringer.

The defendant Dexing, as the registered shipowner of the "Golden Sun" and the actual carrier of the plaintiff LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO's cargo, should have carried the cargo to the port of destination in accordance with the terms of the bill of lading. However, Dexing seriously violated international shipping practices by issuing two sets of bills of lading for the same cargo, unilaterally changing the port of discharge, and selling the plaintiff's cargo to others. Its conduct infringed the plaintiff's right of ownership over the cargo. Article 106, paragraph 2, of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "Citizens and legal persons who through their fault encroach upon the property of the state or a collective, or upon the property or person of another person, shall bear civil liability." Dexing shall compensate the plaintiff for all losses suffered as a result. Because the cargo in this case has been auctioned by Zhanjiang Customs, it is impossible to return the cargo to LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO. Therefore, Dexing shall compensate the plaintiff for the contractual price of the cargo, USD 1,692,282, together with interest.

The defendant Qinglong Branch, having been entrusted by the defendant Dexing, had its employees demand payment of freight on behalf of Dexing. Qinglong Branch also, in accordance with the faxed instructions from Dexing, confirmed the validity of the second set of bills of lading. The consequences of the above acts of Qinglong Branch shall be borne by the principal, Dexing. Except for the fact that employees of Qinglong Branch used notepaper bearing the letterhead of the defendant Qinglong Head Office when demanding freight for Dexing, Qinglong Head Office has no connection with this case. The plaintiff LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO's claim that Qinglong Head Office is the actual owner of the "Golden Sun" does not comply with Article 9 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "the acquisition, transfer, and extinction of ownership of a ship shall be registered with the ship registration authorities; without registration, the same shall not be asserted against a third party." The claim that Qinglong Branch is the actual operator of the "Golden Sun" lacks sufficient evidence and cannot be supported. LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO has neither proven that Qinglong Head Office and Qinglong Branch shared a common intent to defraud with Dexing, nor proven that Qinglong Head Office and Qinglong Branch committed acts of fraud against LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO. Therefore, LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO's request to hold Qinglong Head Office and Qinglong Branch liable for infringement is insufficiently grounded and is not supported.

In conclusion, the Guangzhou Maritime Court rendered the following judgment on December 29, 1998:

1. The defendant Dexing shall compensate the plaintiff LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO for the cargo loss of USD 1,692,282 together with interest.

2. The claims of the plaintiff LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO against the defendants Qinglong Head Office and Qinglong Branch are dismissed.

Court acceptance fee of USD 18,460 shall be borne by the defendant Dexing; property preservation application fee and execution fee of USD 9,520 shall be borne by the plaintiff LA FILIPINAUY GONGCO.
